title: Man Utd’s Heaviest Champions League Defeats of All Time
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray7:05 AM EDTMan Utd recently added to their list of worst European defeats. / Image Photo Agency/Getty ImagesManchester United have been one of the Champions League’s key protagonists since the competition’s rebranding in 1992.

Despite their fall from grace following the departure of Sir Alex Ferguson in 2013, the Red Devils remain among Europe’s leading clubs and, naturally, have an overwhelmingly impressive record in the continent’s premier tournament.

However, there have been a fair few off-days, too. Even a club with the stature and reputation of United is occasionally humiliated on the European stage—as was the case during their recent trip to Como.
With that in mind, here are United’s six biggest Champions League defeats.

Man Utd were left stunned by an unfamiliar foe during the 2002–03 season.  / Mike Egerton/EMPICS/Getty ImagesThere were some mitigating factors around United’s shock defeat to Maccabi Haifa in the group stage of the 2002–03 Champions League.
Firstly, the Red Devils had already qualified for the next round of the competition following four straight victories. Secondly, Ferguson fielded an inexperienced and weakened side as a result.
However, having beaten the Israeli side 5–2 at Old Trafford, there were few signs that United would capitulate in such dramatic fashion during the reverse fixture.

Raimondas Žutautas proved the thorn in United’s side as he grabbed an assist and goal either side of the halftime whistle, with his 35-yard strike doubling the home side’s advantage. Eventually, a young Yakubu rounded off the scoring with a penalty in the closing stages.
An undoubtedly surprising result, but one without any consequence.

Man Utd were undone by an individual masterclass. / Jamie McDonald/Getty ImagesMuch like during their bruising defeat to Maccabi Haifa two years earlier, United had already qualified from their Champions League group when traveling to Fenerbahçe for their final outing. Yet again, Ferguson named a makeshift side, which proved unable to cope with one man in particular: Tuncay Şanlı.

The Fenerbahçe forward, who would late venture to England to play for Middlesbrough, Stoke City and Bolton Wanderers, scored a second-half hat trick to secure one of the Turkish side’s most memorable European triumphs.

Two clinical efforts bookended a header as the Türkiye international single-handedly downed United, who were making an unwanted habit of being humiliated during admittedly meaningless European away days.

The eventual champions proved too good at San Siro. / Etsuo Hara/Getty ImagesUnited found themselves one step away from the Champions League final in 2006–07 having motored to the semifinal stage. AC Milan were the final hurdle they had to overcome to reach the showpiece event.

Carlo Ancelotti’s side had reached the final two years earlier, succumbing to Liverpool in that match in Istanbul, and they were fueled by revenge as they once again came up against English opponents.

Kaká’s brilliance hadn’t been enough for the Italians during the first leg at Old Trafford, with Milan losing 3–2 following Wayne Rooney’s brace and a strike from Cristiano Ronaldo. But the Brazilian starred during a 3–0 victory at San Siro in the second leg.

Kaká opened the scoring after just 11 minutes to level the aggregate score, with Clarence Seedorf proceeding to double Milan’s lead on the night after half-an-hour. Alberto Gilardino then secured a place in the final for the Rossoneri in the closing stages.
United would have come up against Liverpool had they reached the final, but at least they witnessed their bitter rivals lose to Milan in Athens.

Lionel Messi humbled the Red Devils. / Etsuo Hara/Getty ImagesUnited had staged a heroic turnaround in the round of 16 of the 2018–19 Champions League to overcome Paris Saint-Germain at Parc des Princes, but a quarterfinal tie with Barcelona proved a step too far for Ole Gunnar Solskjær’s men.
Having been defeated 1–0 at home during the first leg, United journeyed to Camp Nou hoping for another dramatic comeback win, but Lionel Messi ensured there would be no such remontada.
